label: mid/late original-phase input from set {f,j,z,v,1,p,t,c,o,a,m} in a sequence that starts with {h,2,y,g,l,0,b,d}
explanation: Graded, apparently additive unit. 89% of activation mass is in the original phase. It is silent at t=0-1, weak at t=2, and peaks at orig_idx 5-8. Two factors stack. First, the current input: f, j, z, v and 1 are strongest, then p, t, c, o, a, m. Second, the stored prefix: the rate is higher when the first one or two original tokens are h, 2, y, g, l, 0, b or d. The top examples all begin with h/2/g/y and fire on j/f/z. The unit also fires moderately on <DEL> (7.6% of mass), more when the prefix starts with these tokens. It is nearly silent in the copy phase (3.6% of mass, mostly recall_idx 1-2). On first occurrences of a token it fires 1.6x more often than on repeats. Missed activations are weak firings on other tokens or with other prefixes; false positives are mostly cases where the prefix has only one weak H token. Dev: P 0.59, R 0.54, F1 0.56, mass recall 0.69, and coverage rises with activation (0.82 in the top quartile).
